Which countries are actually covered in trees? Look for the darkest greens on this map, then look at where the pale patches are.

a thread 🧵🗺️
1/ The map shows the share of each country's land covered by forest in 2025. Data: Our World in Data (CC BY). Forest here means trees at least five metres tall, excluding agricultural systems.
2/ Globally, forests cover about 4.14 billion hectares, or roughly 31% of the world's land, according to the FAO's 2025 assessment.
3/ The darkest greens sit in the Guianas and Gabon. Suriname was about 94% forest in 2023, and Gabon about 91%, per FAO figures.
4/ Size matters as much as share. Russia, Brazil, Canada, the US and China together hold about 54% of the world's forests.
5/ Now the pale patches: the Sahara, the Arabian peninsula and Central Asia are nearly white. Little forest cover is what you'd expect in dry climates.
6/ Net forest loss has slowed, from 7.8 million hectares a year in the 1990s to about 4.7 million a year in 2010-2020. That's still a net loss.
7/ Does this map match what you expected? Follow @forummapping for more maps like this.
